haiku-low.q1: No incident is open for the service and rule, and the breach streak would reach 3 consecutive breach ticks (above 2 percent on at least 500 requests).
haiku-low.q2: Each breaching tick adds one to the incident's breach count, sets last breach time, and resets the clean streak to 0. No page is sent.
haiku-low.q3: Ten consecutive clean ticks resolve it, with resolved notices and pending escalations cancelled. A later breach opens a new incident with fresh streaks and a new level 1 page.
haiku-low.q4: Level 1 (primary) pages when the incident opens. Level 2 (secondary) pages 5 minutes later, and level 3 (manager) 5 minutes after that, unless acknowledged or resolved.
haiku-low.q5: Push failure sends SMS to the same person. If both fail, the page is marked failed and retried with backoff for unsucceeded channels only; escalation continues on schedule.
haiku-low.q6: Everyone with a page row for the incident gets a resolved notice, using the people recorded on those rows. Pending escalation jobs are cancelled in the same transaction.
haiku-low.q7: Kept in the rule_state table, one row per service and rule. A non-breach resets the breach streak to 0; a breach, between, or opening resets the clean streak; resolving resets both.
haiku-low.q8: Each tick is claimed by inserting a tick_claims row keyed on service, rule and minute, so only one insert wins. Fenced transactions write nothing if the lease expired, and a partial unique index allows one open incident.
haiku-low.q9: Each level's job is triggered when it is due, 5 minutes after the previous level's commit. It re-reads the incident and pages only if still open and not acknowledged.
haiku-low.q10: The provider calls the webhook with the provider page ID. A valid signature finds the page and incident, sets acked_at and acked_by if empty, and cancels pending escalation jobs in a locked transaction.
haiku-low.q11: The person is chosen at page time from the on-call schedule lookup for that level. If the lookup fails, the last successful roster slot is used, and the chosen person is then stored on the page row.
haiku-low.q12: It reads the person IDs recorded on the incident's page rows, not a new schedule lookup, so a handover cannot change who hears about the resolution.

sonnet.q1: No incident is open for that service and rule, and the tick is a breach (error rate above 2% on at least 500 requests in the 5-minute window) that makes the breach streak reach 3 consecutive breach ticks.
sonnet.q2: No new incident or page. The open incident gets breach count + 1 and last breach time set, and the clean streak is reset to 0, all in a fenced transaction that marks the tick done.
sonnet.q3: 10 consecutive clean ticks (error rate below 1% on at least 500 requests) resolve it. Between resets the clean streak to 0, and low volume leaves it unchanged. The same transaction sets both streaks to 0, cancels pending escalation jobs and queues resolved notices. A later breach starts a new incident with both streaks at 0 and level 1 starting fresh.
sonnet.q4: Primary (level 1) is paged at incident open. The secondary (level 2) is paged 5 minutes after the level-1 commit. The engineering manager (level 3, the last level) is paged 5 minutes after the level-2 commit. Each level goes out only if the incident is still open and not acknowledged.
sonnet.q5: If the push fails (error or timeout), the send job sends an SMS to the same person. If push and SMS both fail, the page row is marked failed and the send job retries with backoff, sending only channels that haven't succeeded. Retries stop on success, or for a page when the incident resolves or is acked. A resolved notice keeps retrying until a channel succeeds. Escalation continues on schedule. A provider fully down also raises a non-paging alarm. The number of retries and the backoff length are not set. A page with no person sends nothing and is not retried.
sonnet.q6: Everyone paged for the incident gets a resolved notice, including the person who acked. It is one send job per recorded page row, using the people recorded on the page rows. Pending escalation jobs are cancelled in the same transaction as the resolution, and any job that still runs re-reads the incident, sees it resolved and drops itself.
sonnet.q7: In the rule_state table in the shared transactional database, one row per service and rule, holding breach_streak and clean_streak. The breach streak is reset to 0 by any non-breach result, by a failed metrics query (missed tick), and when an incident opens. The clean streak is reset to 0 by a breach or between tick while an incident is open. Resolving sets both to 0. Low volume leaves the clean streak unchanged.
sonnet.q8: Only the evaluator that wins the tick claim (insert, or one conditional-update takeover of an expired lease) evaluates the tick. Every decision is a fenced transaction that writes nothing if the evaluator no longer holds an unexpired claim. A pair's ticks run in order. A partial unique index on (service, rule) where status is open allows only one open incident. If the insert is rejected, the breach is recorded on the existing incident and nothing is queued. A unique (incident_id, level) key also blocks a second page for a level.
sonnet.q9: Each step is a durable job in the jobs table. The level-2 job is queued at incident open with a due time of now + 5 min, and the level-3 job is queued by a successful level-2 commit. When due, the job re-reads the incident. If it is open and not acknowledged, it looks up the person, then in one transaction it locks the incident row, rechecks open and not acked, inserts the page row, queues the next-level job (none after level 3) and queues the send job. Otherwise it drops.
sonnet.q10: The provider calls our webhook with the provider page ID after the responder taps Acknowledge. The webhook checks the signature (invalid gives 401 and no change). It finds the page by provider page ID and gets the incident from it. An unknown ID gets 200, is logged, and changes nothing. In one transaction it locks the incident row, sets acked_at and acked_by if empty, and marks the incident's pending escalation jobs cancelled. Pending escalation jobs are cancelled, and any job that still runs rechecks and drops.
sonnet.q11: At escalation or opening time, just before the transaction that creates that level's page row, by looking up the schedule outside any transaction. The primary is looked up when the incident opens, the secondary when the level-2 job runs, and the manager when the level-3 job runs. If the lookup fails, the roster slot for that level from the last successful lookup is used. If it is empty, the page has no person and an alarm is raised. The person is fixed on the page row at that time.
sonnet.q12: It reads the person IDs recorded on the incident's page rows, with no new schedule lookup, so a handover can't change who is told. A resolved notice is a send job of kind resolved, one per recorded page, and creates no page row.
